title: Quasi-regular sequences with flat quotient survive arbitrary base change
statement:
Let $R\to A$ and $R\to R'$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. Let $b\geq0$, $f_1,\ldots,f_b\in A$, $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$, and $C=A/J$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Assume that $C$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and that the canonical graded $C$-algebra homomorphism
$$C[T_1,\ldots,T_b]\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_J(A),\qquad T_j\longmapsto[f_j]_1,$$
is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Put $A'=A\otimes_RR'$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], with multiplication $(a\otimes r)(a_1\otimes r_1)=aa_1\otimes rr_1$ and unit $1\otimes1$, and put $f'_j=f_j\otimes1$, $J'=(f'_1,\ldots,f'_b)$, and $C'=A'/J'$. Then the canonical graded $C'$-algebra homomorphism
$$C'[T_1,\ldots,T_b]\longrightarrow\operatorname{gr}_{J'}(A'),\qquad T_j\longmapsto[f'_j]_1,$$
is an isomorphism. No flatness of $R\to R'$, flatness of $R\to A$, finite-presentation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, part (1); quasi-regularity is the displayed isomorphism of algebra.tex Tag 061P.

proof.text: Put $G_m=J^m/J^{m+1}$ for $m\geq0$. Let $S_m$ be the finite set of tuples $\alpha\in\mathbf N^b$ with $|\alpha|=m$: each coordinate lies between $0$ and $m$, so this is a subset of $\{0,\ldots,m\}^b$. The assumed graded isomorphism restricts in degree $m$ to the $C$-linear isomorphism $C^{S_m}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_m$ sending the coordinate vector $e_\alpha$ to $[f^\alpha]$. This follows from the monomial description in [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and the homogeneous components in [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Hence $G_m$ is flat over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-product-flat-modules], since $C$ is flat. Flatness passes across this isomorphism: the induced tensor maps are inverse on pure tensors, so injectivity is unchanged. The empty set $S_m$ gives the zero module, which is covered by the finite-product lemma.

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, proof of part (1), lines 8004-8012; notation R,A,R' here corresponds to A,B,A' there.

proof.text: For $m\geq1$ put $Q_m=A/J^m$. We prove by induction on $m\geq1$ that $Q_m$ is flat over $R$. The base case is $Q_1=C$, flat by hypothesis. At the induction step the quotient maps give $0\to G_m\xrightarrow{i}Q_{m+1}\xrightarrow{q}Q_m\to0$: a class of $a\in A$ maps to zero in $Q_m$ exactly when $a\in J^m$, and its class in $Q_{m+1}$ depends on $a$ modulo $J^{m+1}$. Thus the kernel is precisely $G_m$, with the indicated injection. These identifications use [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] and [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. Step 1 supplies flatness of $G_m$; the induction hypothesis supplies flatness of $Q_m$.

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, proof of part (1), lines 8004-8012; notation R,A,R' here corresponds to A,B,A' there.

proof.text: Fix this induction step and any injection $u:X\hookrightarrow Y$ of $R$-modules. Tensor the short exact sequence of Step 2 on the left with $X$ and $Y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] both rows are short exact because their last term $Q_m$ is flat. If $z\in X\otimes_RQ_{m+1}$ dies in $Y\otimes_RQ_{m+1}$, its image in $X\otimes_RQ_m$ vanishes by flatness of $Q_m$. Exactness lifts $z$ to $w\in X\otimes_RG_m$. The image of $w$ in $Y\otimes_RG_m$ is zero, since its image in the middle of the bottom row is zero and that row starts with an injection. Flatness of $G_m$ now gives $w=0$, hence $z=0$. Commutativity of these squares is the equality on pure tensors $x\otimes v\mapsto u(x)\otimes i(v)$ or $u(x)\otimes q(v)$, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. By [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] this proves $Q_{m+1}$ flat, completing the induction. This is the explicit flat-extension chase behind Algebra Tag 00HM, lemma-flat-ses, first assertion; it uses only the cited flat-quotient exactness and the definition of flatness.

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, proof of part (1), lines 8004-8012; notation R,A,R' here corresponds to A,B,A' there.

proof.text: For every $m\geq0$ let $u_m:J^m\otimes_RR'\to A'$ send $x\otimes s$ to $x\otimes s$ in $A'$. Its image is an ideal: multiplication by $a\otimes t$ sends $x\otimes s$ to $ax\otimes ts$, and arbitrary elements are finite sums of pure tensors. For $m\geq1$, the definition of ideal multiplication in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] implies that $J^m$ is generated by the $f^\alpha$ with $|\alpha|=m$, by expanding a product of $m$ elements of the generated ideal. Every $x\otimes s$ in the image is consequently a finite sum of $(a\otimes s)(f^\alpha\otimes1)$; conversely $f^\alpha\otimes1$ lies in the image. Therefore $\operatorname{im}u_m=J'^m$. For $m=0$, $u_0:A\otimes_RR'\to A'$ is the identity and its image is $A'=J'^0$. This uses only the tensor generators of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] and the multiplication specified in the item.

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, proof of part (1), lines 8004-8012; notation R,A,R' here corresponds to A,B,A' there.

proof.text: For $m\geq1$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] to $0\to J^m\to A\to Q_m\to0$, tensoring with $R'$. Its last term is flat by Steps 2-3. The tensor order can be reversed by $s\otimes x\mapsto x\otimes s$, whose inverse is the same formula in the other direction, well defined by the balanced relations of [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. It follows that $u_m$ is injective. Combined with Step 4, $u_m$ identifies $J^m\otimes_RR'$ with the actual submodule $J'^m\subseteq A'$. The case $m=0$ is the identity. In particular the case $m=1$ identifies $C\otimes_RR'$ with $C'=A'/J'$ via $\bar a\otimes s\mapsto\overline{a\otimes s}$. The map is a ring isomorphism: it is bijective by exactness, and respects products and the unit on pure tensors by the multiplication specified in the item and the quotient operations of [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient].

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, proof of part (1), lines 8004-8012; notation R,A,R' here corresponds to A,B,A' there.

proof.text: Tensor $J^{m+1}\to J^m\to G_m\to0$ with $R'$ for each $m\geq0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], its last term is the cokernel of the first arrow. Under the injections of Step 5 the first arrow is exactly the inclusion $J'^{m+1}\to J'^m$: on a generator $x\otimes s$ both composites into $A'$ give $x\otimes s$. Thus the cokernel identification gives a bijective linear map $\beta_m:G_m\otimes_RR'\xrightarrow{\sim}J'^m/J'^{m+1}$ with $\beta_m([x]\otimes s)=[x\otimes s]$. This formula is balanced and respects the quotient, since a representative from $J^{m+1}$ maps into $J'^{m+1}$. It is $C'$-linear under $C'=C\otimes_RR'$ from Step 5: on pure coefficient tensors, both orders of multiplication send $(\bar a\otimes t)([x]\otimes s)$ to $[ax\otimes ts]$, using [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring].

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, proof of part (1), lines 8004-8012; notation R,A,R' here corresponds to A,B,A' there.

proof.text: Tensor the isomorphism $C^{S_m}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_m$ of Step 1 with $R'$. It stays invertible without a flatness hypothesis: tensor its inverse and use compatibility with composition from [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. There is a direct coordinate isomorphism $(C^{S_m})\otimes_RR'\xrightarrow{\sim}(C\otimes_RR')^{S_m}$, taking $v\otimes s$ to $(v_\alpha\otimes s)_\alpha$. Its inverse includes each coordinate into the tensor by $(c\otimes s)_\alpha\mapsto(ce_\alpha)\otimes s$ and sums over the finite set $S_m$. The two composites are identities on pure tensors and coordinate vectors. Using Step 5 and composing with $\beta_m$, this gives a $C'$-linear bijection $C'^{S_m}\xrightarrow{\sim}J'^m/J'^{m+1}$ which sends $e_\alpha$ to $[f'^\alpha]$; indeed $f^\alpha\otimes1=f'^\alpha$ by the multiplication of $A'$. Its scalar extension to arbitrary coordinate coefficients uses the $C'$-linearity checked in Step 6. By [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], this is precisely the degree-$m$ part of the canonical polynomial homomorphism in the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0CEP, lemma-relative-regular-immersion-algebra, proof of part (1), lines 8004-8012; notation R,A,R' here corresponds to A,B,A' there.

proof.text: The canonical homomorphism is graded and its degree-$m$ part is bijective by Step 7. It is therefore bijective on the whole ring: a polynomial in its kernel has each homogeneous part zero by injectivity in that degree, while an element of the target is a finite sum of homogeneous components by [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], and choosing preimages of these finitely many components gives a polynomial preimage. The inverse of this bijective algebra homomorphism is an algebra homomorphism, since applying the injective original map verifies addition, multiplication, scalar multiplication and the unit. Hence it is the required canonical graded $C'$-algebra isomorphism. This also covers $b=0$ (only the degree-zero monomial remains) and $C'=0$ (every coefficient and homogeneous piece is zero).

Step 6: right exactness gives G_m tensor R' = J'^m/J'^{m+1}, C'-linearly. Steps 7-8: the degree-m map sends e_alpha to [f'^alpha], and degreewise bijectivity gives the algebra isomorphism. proof_deps is the union of the steps' uses. All cited nodes are definitions or Mathlib leaves (sk-thm-p1), so no tool_uses entry is needed and none was accepted.
